mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, resulting in higher present values and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings growth and investor confidence, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST are rising.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), strong labor market conditions support consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.0%, it signals economic weakness that reduces corporate earnings growth and investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) reflects strong consumer demand and economic activity, supporting corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1200.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates robust manufacturing and labor market expansion, driving corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when both INDPRO and PAYEMS are increasing.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 315), aggressive monetary tightening to combat inflation increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 315.
